$comment: Every named dataset the mock can serve, and how one is composed from another. A scenario that differs from populated in three endpoints holds three files; degraded holds none at all, because it is populated plus a declaration of which endpoints misbehave. Adding a scenario here requires no change to the console.

scenarios.name: populated
scenarios.description: A full deployment mid-operation: ninety-odd resources, open incidents, waiting approvals, running and completed runs, episodes, a topology and an audit trail.

scenarios.name: empty
scenarios.description: A brand-new deployment with nothing in it. Every screen shows its empty state, which is how the empty states get reviewed at all.

scenarios.name: first-run
scenarios.description: Configured and not finished: the organisation exists, no provider is configured, no integration holds a credential, and readiness says so. This is what the setup checklist renders against.

scenarios.name: degraded
scenarios.description: The populated deployment with individual endpoints misbehaving in declared ways, so panel-level error handling is exercised on every screen that fetches.

scenarios.name: incident-live
scenarios.description: A run in flight, streaming. The longer event sequence the live layer's reducer is proved against, including the point a reconnection lands in the middle of a turn.

scenarios.name: restricted
scenarios.description: The same deployment seen by a viewer. The data does not change; what may be done with it does, which is what the role matrix screens are for.

scenarios.name: audit-flooded
scenarios.description: The same deployment, its audit trail dominated by two hundred entries from its own automation principal against a total far larger still — the shape that hides every real event behind a count nothing on screen explains.

scenarios.name: scale
scenarios.description: Ten thousand runs, ten thousand events, ten thousand resources and a five-hundred-node configuration tree. Generated from a fixed seed rather than committed, so a measurement taken against it today is comparable with one taken last month.

scenarios.name: now-violations
scenarios.description: The populated deployment with one run and one incident carrying the five ways a 'Now' screen has been found to mislead a reader — a raw report standing in for a title, a hexadecimal id standing in for a name, two fallbacks in one line, a live control on a run the list already called done, and a chip that answers from a read that failed. Exists to give the transversal suite's bans on those screens a reproducible red, so their gate does not depend on a shared, changing staging environment ever being in the wrong state again.
